headline: Bangladesh emerging team earns hard-fought draw against South Africa in first four-day match
summary: Despite a batting collapse in their second innings, Bangladesh's emerging cricketers showed resilience to secure a draw against South Africa in the opening four-day match of their series. The team will look to carry this fighting spirit into the next match.
details: Bangladesh emerging team secured a hard-fought draw in the first four-day match of their series against South Africa emerging team in Potchefstroom. The match concluded on Wednesday with key performances from Mahidul Islam Ankon, Aminul Islam Biplob, and Nayeem Hasan.

Resuming their second innings on the final day at 15-0 and needing 396 more runs to win, Bangladesh faced a significant challenge. The team's batting order faltered, losing five wickets for just 70 runs, putting them in deep trouble.
However, a crucial 105-run partnership for the sixth wicket between Aminul Islam Biplob and Mahidul Islam Ankon steadied the innings. Biplob contributed 74 runs off 147 balls before his dismissal.

Following Biplob's departure, Ankon and Nayeem Hasan formed an unbeaten 69-run partnership for the seventh wicket, guiding Bangladesh to 244-6. Ankon remained not out on 48 from 208 balls, while Nayeem scored an unbeaten 49 off 79 deliveries, ultimately leading to the draw.

Earlier in the match, South Africa emerging had declared their second innings at 130-4 on day three, setting Bangladesh a challenging target of 411. Bangladesh had been bowled out for 239 in their first innings.
South Africa had posted a formidable 519-5 declared in their first innings, with captain van Buuren scoring 171 and Seletswane remaining unbeaten on 150.
The second and final four-day match of the series is scheduled to begin on Sunday at Willowmoore Park in Benoni.

Following Biplob's departure, Ankon and Nayeem Hasan formed an unbeaten 69-run partnership for the seventh wicket, guiding Bangladesh to 244-6. Ankon remained not out on 48 from 208 balls, while Nayeem scored an unbeaten 49 off 79 deliveries, ultimately leading to the draw.

Earlier in the match, South Africa emerging had declared their second innings at 130-4 on day three, setting Bangladesh a challenging target of 411. Bangladesh had been bowled out for 239 in their first innings.
